chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ḥanān, who said:
ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was sitting there, and he said to him: Inform me—may I be made your ransom—about the salat of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

He عليه السلام said to him: "The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform eight rakʿahs at zawāl, and four for the first prayer, and eight after it, and four for al-ʿaṣr, and three for al-maghrib, and four after al-maghrib, and four for al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah, and eight for salat al-layl, and three for al-watr, and the two rakʿahs of al-fajr, and salat al-ghadāh as two rakʿahs."

I said: May I be made your ransom, if I am stronger and able to do more than this, would Allah punish me for the abundance of salat? He said: "No, but He punishes for abandoning the sunnah (prophetic tradition)."

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday decline of the sun, indicating the time of the noon nawāfil
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the established prophetic tradition and recommended practice
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, referring here to the two rakʿahs before the morning obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْوَتْرَ: the concluding odd-numbered prayer of the night prayer sequence
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, referring to the Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed during the night
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: salat (prayer), referring here to the Prophet’s prescribed pattern of prayer

ai.seo_question: What was the daily pattern of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله recommended prayers, and is praying more than that blameworthy?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the pattern of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله recommended daily and nightly prayers, listing the rakʿahs associated with each time. It also clarifies that abundance in salat is not blameworthy, while abandoning the established sunnah (prophetic tradition) is what incurs blame.
